stories.head: Colombian forces end Cartagena supermarket siege, freeing all hostages
stories.say: Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in Cartagena early on Wednesday, ending a siege of about seventeen hours. The president says every hostage was freed.
stories.stand: President Abelardo de la Espriella said one hostage-taker was killed in the raid, which followed a failed armoured-vehicle robbery.
body: Colombian security forces stormed an Éxito supermarket in Cartagena shortly after midnight on Wednesday, ending a standoff of about 17 hours. President Abelardo de la Espriella said all hostages were rescued and one hostage-taker was killed.
Authorities said the siege began after a failed attempt to rob an armoured vehicle. About 10 people, including several elderly women, were released during negotiations before the raid.
The president travelled to Cartagena during the crisis and ruled out guerrilla or paramilitary involvement, calling the captors criminals. The city's airport suspended landings for about 45 minutes.

stories.head: Fuel tanker fire on Cairo ring road kills at least 30
stories.say: At least thirty people were killed on Wednesday when a fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on Cairo's ring road. Egypt's health minister says the toll could rise.
stories.stand: Egyptian officials say the blaze in Waraq set more than two dozen vehicles alight; the health minister called the toll preliminary.
body: At least 30 people were killed on Wednesday when a truck carrying fuel overturned on the Ring Road in Waraq, Greater Cairo, and caught fire, Egyptian officials said.
The public prosecutor's office said at least 25 people were injured and more than two dozen cars and motorcycles were burned. DNA tests are under way to identify victims.
Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar called the death toll preliminary and said he would visit the scene. President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi offered condolences.

stories.head: Israeli strike kills Hamas security official and family in Gaza
stories.say: An Israeli air strike on the Shati camp in Gaza killed a Hamas internal security official, his wife and two teenage daughters on Wednesday, Gaza's interior ministry says.
stories.stand: The strike came less than a day after the head of Hamas's internal security service was killed, Gaza officials said.
body: An Israeli air strike on a home in the Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, killed Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf at dawn on Wednesday, Gaza's interior ministry said. It said he led the internal security service in northern Gaza.
The ministry said his wife and their daughters, aged 15 and 13, were also killed. The strike came less than 24 hours after the killing of the service's director general, Naim Abu Nahal.
Hamas called on the countries guaranteeing the ceasefire to intervene. The report did not include a response from Israel's military.

stories.head: Bodies recovered from flooded illegal gold mine in West Java
stories.say: Rescuers in Indonesia have recovered at least eight bodies from a flooded illegal gold mine in West Java, and more miners are still missing after a river burst into the pit on Monday.
stories.stand: The 100-metre-deep pit in Bogor district flooded after torrential rain; officials say the water will take a long time to drain.
body: An unauthorised open-pit gold mine in the Pongkor area of Bogor district, West Java, flooded on Monday when a nearby river overflowed after heavy rain. The mine is 100 metres deep.
Rescuers had recovered at least eight bodies by Wednesday, Australia's ABC reported. Police said 11 miners got out before the shaft flooded.

Desiana Kartika Bahari, head of the Jakarta search and rescue office, said the water had not receded and would take a long time to drain. State miner Antam said the site was not part of its operations.

stories.head: Saudi Arabia says it downed Houthi drones over Ras Tanura refinery
stories.say: Saudi Arabia says it shot down four Houthi drones over its Ras Tanura refinery on Wednesday, a day after the Saudi-led coalition struck the Yemeni port of Hodeidah.
stories.stand: The Houthis said they hit the refinery and threatened Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah, after the coalition's strike on Hodeidah.
body: Saudi air defences destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura in the Eastern Province on Wednesday morning, coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki said. He said fragments fell but no casualties were reported.
The Houthis claimed an attack on the refinery and said it caused fires. Their spokesperson, Yahya Saree, also urged workers at Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah, to evacuate.

The coalition struck Hodeidah, the main port for supplies into Houthi-held northern Yemen, on Tuesday. On the same day a Houthi drone hit Riyadh's tallest tower, injuring at least 11 people, Saudi authorities said.

stories.head: Two Libyan officers die after Ukrainian drone strike on Russian ships
stories.say: Two Libyan naval officers have died of wounds from Sunday's Ukrainian drone strike on Russian ships at Benghazi, and eastern Libya's army says it will retaliate.
stories.stand: Kyiv calls the vessels legitimate targets; Libya's rival governments have both protested, and the UN warned against foreign conflicts spreading there.
body: Two officers of the Libyan National Army died on Tuesday of wounds from a Ukrainian drone attack on Russian vessels at Benghazi's naval base on Sunday, the LNA said. Its command vowed to respond at a time of its choosing.
Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, said both ships were valid targets and called the strike legitimate self-defence. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Kyiv was behind it.

The eastern government asked the UN for an international investigation, and the Tripoli government demanded an explanation from Ukraine. France's foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, backed Ukraine's right to self-defence.

stories.head: US tells its citizens to leave Iran immediately
stories.say: The US Virtual Embassy in Iran has told American citizens to leave the country immediately, warning on Wednesday that hostilities could escalate quickly.
stories.stand: The alert says Iran, the Houthis and aligned groups may target US interests and citizens across the region.
body: The US Virtual Embassy in Iran issued a security alert on Wednesday telling US citizens to leave Iran immediately and not to travel there for any reason. It warned that hostilities could escalate quickly.

The alert said Iran, the Houthis and aligned groups may target US interests and citizens in the region, including companies and institutions. It advised people to prepare for flight cancellations and airspace closures.
The US and Iran have had no diplomatic relations since 1980. Switzerland acts as the protecting power for US citizens in Iran.

stories.head: Russian drones kill seven in Ukraine as Kyiv hits three refineries
stories.say: Russian drone strikes killed at least seven people across Ukraine overnight into Wednesday, while Ukraine says its drones hit three Russian oil refineries.
stories.stand: Ukraine's air force says it downed 88 of 112 drones; Russian governors confirmed attacks in Samara and Rostov regions.
body: Russia launched 112 drones overnight into Wednesday, Ukraine's air force said, and 88 were shot down or neutralised. Authorities said at least seven people were killed, including one on a minibus in Kharkiv region.
A Naftogaz gas production site in Poltava region was hit and stopped work. Energy facilities in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions were also struck, causing power cuts.

Ukrainian monitoring sources said drones hit three refineries in Russia. Samara's governor, Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, confirmed an attack and one death, and Rostov's governor said a plant in Novoshakhtinsk stopped work.

stories.head: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat and shuts Bern's new office
stories.say: North Korea has ordered Switzerland to close its new office in Pyongyang and given its head forty-eight hours to leave, in retaliation for Swiss sanctions on a children's camp.
stories.stand: Pyongyang declared the head of mission persona non grata five weeks after the office reopened.
body: North Korea ordered Switzerland to close its newly opened office in Pyongyang and gave its head, Astier Sylvain, 48 hours to leave, state agency KCNA reported on Wednesday.
Pyongyang said it was retaliating for Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp in Wonsan. Switzerland says the camp hosts Ukrainian children taken from Russian-occupied areas.
The office reopened about five weeks earlier. The Swiss foreign ministry said on Tuesday that it wanted to keep dialogue open and that the office was separate from its sanctions policy.

President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan is due in Tripoli on 8 to 9 December for a Turkey-Africa summit. It would be his first visit to Libya in 15 years.

stories.say: Thousands of teachers marched past Chile's presidential palace on Tuesday in a nationwide strike against education cuts proposed by President José Antonio Kast's government.
stories.stand: Police in Santiago used water cannon on some protesters, who want more money for public schools and universities.
body: Teachers held a nationwide strike on Tuesday against proposed cuts in Chile's 2027 education budget. Thousands marched in Santiago past La Moneda, the presidential palace.
Police used water cannon to disperse the crowd, and some protesters threw stones at police vehicles, Euronews reported.
The protesters want better funding for public schools and universities. The government of President José Antonio Kast has proposed cuts to several education programmes.

stories.head: Greek strike over living costs grounds flights and halts ferries
stories.say: About fourteen thousand people marched in Athens on Wednesday during a twenty-four-hour strike over living costs, police said. Ferries stayed in port and regional flights were grounded.
stories.stand: Unions for civil servants, dockworkers and teachers called the walkout as Greek inflation hit 5.7% in October.
body: About 14,000 people marched in Athens on Wednesday, according to police, during a 24-hour strike over rising living costs and stagnant wages. There were also protests in Thessaloniki.
Ferries stayed in port, the Athens metro was disrupted and flights to and from 15 regional airports were grounded. Unions representing civil servants, dockworkers and teachers called the strike.
Annual inflation reached 5.7% in October, the statistics authority Elstat said. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis has pledged to raise the monthly minimum wage to €1,000 in early 2028 if re-elected.

stories.head: Lubanga's rebels pull back from near Bunia in DR Congo
stories.say: A rebel group led by Thomas Lubanga says it has pulled back from areas near Bunia in north-eastern Congo after heavy fighting, citing talks mediated by Uganda's president.
stories.stand: The fighting forced health workers to evacuate near Bunia, disrupting the response to Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak.
body: The Convention for the Popular Revolution, led by Thomas Lubanga, said on Tuesday it had withdrawn from areas it recently seized near Bunia, capital of Ituri province. A day earlier it took Iga-Barriere, about 25km north of the city.
The group said it acted out of respect for commitments made in talks with the government mediated by Uganda's president, Yoweri Museveni.

The WHO said on Sunday that fighting near a hospital north of Bunia forced health workers to evacuate, disrupting the Ebola response. Lubanga was convicted by the International Criminal Court in 2012 of using child soldiers.

stories.say: A building under construction collapsed in Karachi on Wednesday, killing at least three people, rescue officials said. About fifteen workers were feared trapped.
stories.stand: Rescue 1122 crews pulled one survivor from the wreckage; authorities are investigating the cause.
body: A multi-storey building under construction collapsed in Karachi, Pakistan, on Wednesday. Rescue 1122, the emergency service, said at least three people were killed and 14 injured.

Crews used heavy machinery and cut three access routes into the wreckage, and one survivor was pulled out alive. About 15 workers were feared trapped, though officials said the number missing was unconfirmed.
Authorities are investigating the cause of the collapse.

stories.say: America's air safety board chair says Army helicopter training flights near Reagan National Airport could resume as soon as the first of December, ten months after a deadly collision.
stories.stand: The FAA says it has had no formal request; senators warn the flights should not restart until new safety measures are in place.
body: Army helicopter training flights near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport could resume as early as Tuesday 1 December, NTSB chair Jennifer Homendy said. The Army has not announced a timeline.
The FAA said it had not received a formal request and must approve any flights. In January 2025 an Army helicopter collided with an American Airlines jet near the airport, killing 67 people.
Senator Maria Cantwell called resuming the flights the wrong direction. Senator Ted Cruz said a House-Senate deal in principle would require aircraft to show nearby traffic with alerts.

stories.head: Two men in court over break-in at William and Kate's Anmer Hall
stories.say: Two men have appeared in court in Norwich accused of breaking into Anmer Hall, the Prince and Princess of Wales's Norfolk home, and stealing cufflinks and a clock.
stories.stand: Prosecutors allege the men climbed a drainpipe into a dressing room; neither entered a plea and both were remanded in custody.
body: Two men appeared at Norwich Magistrates' Court on Wednesday charged over a break-in at Anmer Hall on the Sandringham estate. Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, are charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site.

The court heard they allegedly climbed a drainpipe into a dressing room and took six pairs of cufflinks and a clock. They were arrested in woodland about two kilometres away after a member of staff spotted them, the court heard.
Neither man was asked to enter a plea, and both were remanded in custody. Prosecutors said a third person seen outside has not been arrested. The family was not at the house.

stories.say: MI5's protective security arm has warned British firms that supply Ukraine's armed forces that they could be targeted by Russian sabotage, including arson by proxies.
stories.stand: Russia's embassy denies any plan to attack the UK; the defence ministry is briefing infrastructure and defence leaders.
body: The National Protective Security Authority, part of MI5, issued a notice on Tuesday warning that UK businesses supplying military equipment to Ukraine could be targeted by Russia. It said Russia had increased sabotage attempts against European defence-related sites.

The notice said such attacks often use proxies and low-sophistication methods such as arson. It advised firms to reduce public detail about their work, train staff to spot hostile reconnaissance and rehearse responses.
Russia's embassy in London said it had no plans to attack the UK. The Ministry of Defence is holding closed-door security briefings for defence and infrastructure leaders.

stories.head: Met Police still institutionally racist, misogynistic and homophobic, review finds
stories.say: A review led by Dr Gillian Fairfield finds the Metropolitan Police is still institutionally racist, misogynistic and homophobic, three years after Baroness Casey's report.
stories.stand: The review found no good progress on any Casey recommendation; Sir Mark Rowley says the Met accepts its findings.
body: The Fairfield Review, published on Wednesday, found the Metropolitan Police remains institutionally racist, misogynistic and homophobic. It assessed progress since Baroness Casey's 2023 review.
It found the force had made no good progress on any of Casey's recommendations and said defensiveness was deeply ingrained. Of staff who felt bullied or harassed, 49% did not report it.

Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said the Met accepted the recommendations and that 1,800 officers and staff had been removed since the Casey report. London's mayor, Sadiq Khan, said there should be no spin.

stories.stand: Last-ditch talks over new working arrangements failed; further strikes are planned in December, January and February.
body: RMT members on London Underground are striking from 12pm on Thursday 26 November to 11.59am on Friday, Time Out reported. The dispute is over plans for new working arrangements, and last-ditch talks failed earlier in the week.
There will be no Piccadilly or Circle line services on Thursday, no Waterloo & City service from midday and no Tube services after 9pm. Other lines are reduced from 10am.
Disruption is expected until about 6pm on Friday. London Overground is not affected, and further strikes are planned for 17 and 19 December.

stories.head: 38% of UK Muslim students report Islamophobia at university
stories.say: A survey by the Federation of Student Islamic Societies finds thirty-eight per cent of Muslim students in the UK say they have faced Islamophobia at university.
stories.stand: Most of those affected said they did not feel able to report it, the survey of 715 students at 63 universities found.
body: A survey of 715 students at 63 universities by the Federation of Student Islamic Societies found that 38% of Muslim students had experienced Islamophobia at university. The figure was 42% for women and 34% for men.
Of those affected, 68% did not feel able to report it, and almost half of all respondents did not know how. Three in five said they felt afraid to express views on Palestine.
FOSIS called on universities to adopt a definition of Islamophobia and protect Friday prayers in timetables. The universities contacted had not responded by publication.

body: The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government is considering removing insured tenancy deposit schemes as part of a review of deposit protection, The Negotiator reported. No final decision has been confirmed.

A ministry spokesperson said the schemes did not let the government profit from deposits. Shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said the plan would push up rents.

stories.stand: The panel follows the Hillsborough model and aims to report in time for the 75th anniversary of the first UK test in October 2027.
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced an independent panel to examine the impact of nuclear weapons testing on veterans and their families. It will be chaired by Bishop James Jones, who led the Hillsborough Independent Panel.
Number 10 said it would follow the same model and operate under a legal duty of candour. It aims to deliver an interim report by the 75th anniversary of the first UK test, on 3 October 2027.
Some veterans say they suffered cancers and lost children through miscarriage because of the tests. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he would not prejudge the panel's findings.

He signalled plans to extend protection to freelancers and fans who experience abuse. Campaigner Zelda Perkins called the promises hugely significant.

body: EasyJet's statutory pre-tax profit fell 96% to £24 million in the year to 30 September, from £658 million a year earlier. Headline pre-tax profit fell 89% to £71 million.

body: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has released its first images of Dimorphos, a moonlet about 151 metres wide that NASA's DART probe struck in 2022. They show a large crater on the impacted side.

stories.head: Physicists trap a single antimatter particle for months
stories.say: Northwestern University physicists have trapped a single positron, the antimatter twin of the electron, for months, a step towards comparing matter and antimatter precisely.
stories.stand: The team, led by Gerald Gabrielse, cooled the particle to its quantum ground state; its magnetism has not yet been measured.
body: A team at Northwestern University led by Gerald Gabrielse trapped a single positron, the antimatter counterpart of the electron, and kept it confined for months, according to a study in Physical Review Letters.

The positron was held by electric and magnetic fields in a near-perfect vacuum at about 300 millikelvins. It reached its quantum ground state, and microwaves were used to drive it between energy levels.
The team plans to measure the positron's magnetic moment and compare it with the electron's. The Standard Model predicts no difference, so any gap would point to new physics.

body: Physicists at the University of Queensland sent a message through a brick wall using gravity, according to a study in Science Advances. A lift's 1.8-tonne counterweight was moved between two positions to represent 0 and 1.
A gravimeter on the other side of the wall recovered the word Gravity at 1 bit per minute, so the word took about an hour.
Modelling with quantum sensors suggests a range of about 500 metres at about 15 bits per minute, but this has not been demonstrated. The researchers say the system is far from practical.

The work is purely theoretical and starts from a simplified model. It has not yet been compared with accelerator experiments.

body: About 446,000 fewer people were on PrEP, the HIV prevention drug, in 2025 than in 2024, UNAIDS said in its World AIDS Day report. Only 2.6 million people had access, though more than 20 million could benefit.

stories.say: Alexander Isak scored twice and Florian Wirtz added a long-range goal as Liverpool won three-nil at Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday.
stories.stand: Liverpool now have 12 points from a possible 15 in the league phase; Brugge had the better first-half chances.
body: Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League at the Jan Breydel Stadium on Wednesday. Alexander Isak scored early, finishing first time after Dominik Szoboszlai set him up.
Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 in the 79th minute with a strike from the edge of the box, and Isak added a late third by lifting the ball over goalkeeper Yann Sommer.
The win gives Andoni Iraola's side 12 points from a possible 15. Victor Munoz went off injured in the first half.

stories.head: Lille beat injury-hit Bayern Munich 2-1 for first Champions League win
stories.say: Lille came from behind to beat Bayern Munich two-one, with Ayase Ueda scoring and Aleksandar Pavlović putting through his own net. It's Bayern's first Champions League defeat of the season.
stories.stand: Bayern were without Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Manuel Neuer through injury.
body: Lille beat Bayern Munich 2-1 at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Wednesday. Dayot Upamecano headed Bayern ahead in the 15th minute from a Tom Bischof corner.
Ayase Ueda equalised in the 62nd minute after a run by Nathan Ngoy. Three minutes later Aleksandar Pavlović turned the ball into his own net after Ethan Mbappé's shot hit the post.
It was Lille's first win of the competition and Bayern's first Champions League defeat of the season. Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Manuel Neuer were all injured.

stories.head: Malen penalty earns Roma 2-2 draw at injury-hit PSG
stories.say: Donyell Malen's late penalty earned Roma a two-two draw at Paris Saint-Germain, ending PSG's run of twelve straight wins and their perfect Champions League record.
stories.stand: PSG were without Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia; Ousmane Dembélé had briefly put them ahead from the spot.
body: Roma drew 2-2 at Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday. Mario Hermoso put Roma ahead inside five minutes, and Illia Zabarnyi headed PSG level just after the half-hour.
Substitute Ousmane Dembélé put PSG ahead with a penalty, but Donyell Malen equalised from the spot in the 78th minute after a VAR check.
The draw ended PSG's perfect league-phase record and their 12-match winning run. Real Madrid lead the table with a 100% record.

stories.stand: Luis Suárez scored both Sporting goals; Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time.

stories.head: Raheem Sterling given suspended sentence for dangerous driving
stories.say: Former England winger Raheem Sterling has been given a twelve-month suspended prison sentence for dangerous driving and possessing nitrous oxide, after crashing on the M3 in May.
stories.stand: He must do 100 hours of unpaid work; the judge cited his charity work and engagement with addiction services.
body: Raheem Sterling, 31, was given 12 months' imprisonment suspended for 18 months at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on Wednesday, and ordered to do 100 hours of unpaid work.

He had pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide and failing to provide a blood specimen. In May he crashed his Lamborghini into barriers on the M3. No one else was hurt.
Judge Kirsty Allman said he had shown conscious disregard for other road users, but cited his charity work and engagement with addiction services.

stories.say: The Pittsburgh Steelers have released quarterback Aaron Rodgers, hours after he criticised coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show following his benching.
stories.stand: Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings; Mason Rudolph starts against Denver.
body: The Pittsburgh Steelers released Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, ABC reported, shortly after the four-time NFL MVP criticised coach Mike McCarthy on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show.
The team had announced on Tuesday that Rodgers would be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, with Mason Rudolph starting.

Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings and arriving late, and said the team should release him if it wanted to bench him. Rodgers and McCarthy won a Super Bowl together with Green Bay in 2011.

stories.head: Senegal deny Morocco's claim of contact with CAS arbitrator
stories.say: Senegal's football federation president has called Morocco's claim that he contacted a sports court arbitrator before the AFCON ruling absolutely false.
stories.stand: The Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstated Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions on Tuesday.
body: Morocco's federation claimed that Senegal federation president Abdoulaye Fall had contact with Ulrich Haas, one of three CAS panel members, 48 hours before Tuesday's ruling, AFP reported via Al Jazeera.
Fall told the broadcaster TFM on Wednesday that the claim was absolutely false and that he had never had any exchange with a CAS member.
The CAS panel unanimously reinstated Senegal as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions. Morocco can appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court on procedural grounds.

body: Bayern Munich said Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on 22 April 2025, more than 16 months before his diagnosis was announced, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera.
The club and Musiala's agency issued the statement to address rumours. Bayern said talks with his management on Tuesday were constructive and that his health was the absolute priority.
Musiala was diagnosed in August 2026 with a neurological disorder after collapsing in two games. He has a contract to 2030.

stories.head: 1,220 players register for IPL auction in Goa
stories.say: One thousand two hundred and twenty players have registered for next month's IPL auction in Goa, including eleven from Bangladesh, but not Shakib Al Hasan or Mustafizur Rahman.
stories.stand: Franchises have 66 slots to fill at the auction on 16 December, including 25 for overseas players.
body: An initial list of 1,220 players has been released for the IPL mini auction in Goa on 16 December, AFP reported via Al Jazeera. The BCCI says 66 slots remain, including 25 for overseas players.
Eleven Bangladeshi cricketers registered, led by Towhid Hridoy. Former captain Shakib Al Hasan and fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman are not on the list.
India has 939 players registered, Australia 53 and South Africa 40. England's Ben Stokes is among the high-profile names.

stories.head: Galatasaray reject Israeli complaint to UEFA over Palestine banners
stories.say: Galatasaray's president says the club stands by fans who displayed pro-Palestinian banners, after Israel's government complained to UEFA, calling the complaint political.
stories.stand: Banners at Tuesday's 1-0 win over Aston Villa included Free Palestine; UEFA rules ban political messages at matches.
body: Galatasaray president Dursun Özbek said UEFA had told the club about a complaint from the Israeli government over pro-Palestinian banners shown by fans, Al Jazeera reported. He called the club's stance humanitarian and moral.
Banners at Tuesday's 1-0 home win over Aston Villa included Free Palestine. Turkey's sports minister, Osman Bak, praised the fans.
UEFA's safety rules prohibit political messages in or near stadiums. UEFA had not responded to a request for comment.
